page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual server from the Enhanced instance family, running on a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor features 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and supports vector instructions including AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI. There are no onboard GPUs or local storage devices bundled with the instance, and network throughput is provisioned with a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks show competent single-thread throughput alongside typical constraints associated with a 4-vCPU footprint. The instance registers mid-tier results in single-threaded tests, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1554.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1841.49, and solid gzip compression at 27.89 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is equally steady, assisted by hardware acceleration instructions. However, multi-core and parallel throughput metrics place the instance in the lower percentiles. Geekbench multi-core scored 3302.0, PassMark CPU reached 5840.83, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 20.78 GB/sec. Memory read and write bandwidth hover around 30.43 GB/sec and 25.42 GB/sec respectively for large blocks.

Because the server lacks local disk storage, external block storage must be attached for persistent state, which affects end-to-end I/O latency. From a qualitative resource-efficiency standpoint, the 1:2 memory configuration avoids paying for unused memory when hosting CPU-bound services. The ecs.c7nex.xlarge is technically appropriate for moderately scaled, stateless compute tasks, standard web serving, text and data serialization, proxy nodes, and microservices where single-threaded responsiveness takes precedence over heavy parallel computation.
